transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I keep launching projects and can’t seem to stop. Work plans, certification schedules, upgrades at home, reaching out to old contacts—it gets really intense. I push past normal limits until my wife or my director has to step in and tell me to slow down.
Do these intense periods of activity come and go in distinct phases, or is this how you feel pretty much all the time?

They come in phases. Some weeks I feel almost electric, like I’m unstoppable. But then even a small delay or my wife asking a question can make me snap—I feel like people are deliberately trying to slow me down.
Outside of these energized phases, have you ever had periods where you felt distinctly down, depressed, or lost interest in things?
Yeah. There are stretches where I wake up feeling like a failed version of myself—just heavy and flat. Even answering my wife’s normal questions can feel like too much.
During these energized periods, does your behavior ever severely disrupt your ability to work or manage daily life?

Yeah. The migration failed, and I was put on leave from work. At home, my wife has had to step in about my spending, the late-night work, and when conversations start turning into arguments. I’ve also backed away from church music, climbing, and mentoring because I can’t count on myself to show up or follow through.
During these energized periods, have you ever seen or heard things that other people couldn't see or hear?
Yeah. I’ll hear my name sometimes, or short things like “check the logs” or “they know,” mixed into the server-room hum or from my home office when nobody else is there.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient demonstrates episodic phases of mania characterized by abnormally increased energy and goal-directed activity, irritability, decreased need for sleep, and risky impulsive behaviors (spending). Auditory hallucinations (hearing voices whispering his name and phrases like 'they know') occur during these phases. Combined with a confirmed history of depressive episodes and severe occupational and relationship impairment, the clinical picture fulfills criteria for bipolar affective disorder, current episode manic with psychotic symptoms (F31.2).
